fact_text: Adrien's Singapore tax rate depends on his tax-residency status: if he stays or works in Singapore for 183 days or more in a calendar year, his income is taxed at resident (progressive) rates; below that he is generally a non-resident.
evidence_quote: if you stay or work in Singapore for 183 days or more in a calendar year, your income will be taxed at resident rates for individuals

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A relocating EP holder who arrives mid-year may straddle the 183-day threshold; a continuous stay/work period straddling two calendar years totalling at least 183 days can still qualify him for resident treatment (from YA rules for employees who entered from 1 Jan 2007, excluding directors/public entertainers/professionals).

fact_text: If Adrien is a non-resident for the year, his Singapore employment income is taxed at the higher of a flat 15% or the progressive resident rates; other (non-employment) non-resident income is generally taxed at 24%.
evidence_quote: Employment income of a non-resident individual is taxed at the flat rate of 15% or the progressive resident tax rates, whichever is the higher tax amount

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious for a first mover: it is not simply '15% flat for foreigners'. IRAS compares the flat 15% against the progressive resident computation and applies whichever yields the higher tax. Resident progressive rates top out at 24%.

fact_text: Adrien must file a Singapore Individual Income Tax Return if IRAS notifies him to; e-filing on myTax Portal is due by 18 April (for Year of Assessment 2026, filing opens 1 Mar 2026 and the e-File deadline is 18 Apr 2026).
evidence_quote: you must e-File your Income Tax Return on myTax Portal by 18 Apr 2026

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The Singapore e-file deadline is 18 April (paper filing 15 April), not the 30 April / June deadlines Adrien may expect from France. IRAS assesses on a preceding-calendar-year basis (Year of Assessment).

fact_text: As an Employment Pass holder (a foreigner, not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident), Adrien is not covered by CPF: mandatory CPF contributions are payable only for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
evidence_quote: CPF contributions are payable for Singapore citizens (SCs) and Singapore permanent residents (SPRs) who are: Working in Singapore under a contract of service.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: No CPF means no automatic Singapore retirement/housing/healthcare savings deduction for an EP holder - net-of-tax take-home differs from a local's, and there is no CPF-based social safety net; plan private savings/insurance accordingly. (CPFB separately states CPF contributions are exempted for foreign employees.)

fact_text: When Adrien eventually ceases his Singapore employment, goes on an overseas posting, or leaves Singapore for more than three months, his employer must seek tax clearance by filing Form IR21 at least one month beforehand, and may withhold monies due to him until clearance is given.
evidence_quote: Employers must file Form IR21 at least one month before a non-Singapore Citizen employee ceases employment in Singapore, goes on an overseas posting, or leaves Singapore for more than three months.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Tax clearance (IR21) is an employer obligation triggered on exit, not just at the annual filing. The employer must withhold final monies (salary, bonus, leave pay) until IRAS issues clearance - relevant to Adrien's final pay when he repatriates.

fact_text: France and Singapore have an Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) that can protect Adrien from being taxed twice on the same income, but only tax residents of Singapore or France can claim its benefits, and the specific relief for his situation must be confirmed with a tax adviser.
evidence_quote: Under the Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs), you may be protected from being taxed twice on the same income

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A Singapore-France DTA exists (the revised DTA entered into force in 2016 and has since been modified by the MLI, ratified 19 Jul 2021 - see the IRAS DTA PDF). Whether Adrien can actually claim relief depends on his residency status in each country and the specific article at stake; only Singapore/France tax residents can benefit. Determination is corridor- and case-specific.
